# Bounded parallel read acceptance

Implemented `harness-core/src/test/java/dev/codeharness/core/agent/ParallelReadsTest.java`. No production files changed.

Eight tests verify:

- Explicit safe reads overlap and observed active concurrency never exceeds a configured cap of two across six calls.
- Two reads finish in reverse call order, but transcript and each durable result checkpoint remain in call order on the coordinator thread.
- The assistant checkpoint precedes all read starts. A mutation barrier waits for prior reads; later reads observe the mutation.
- Default options and the six-argument constructor retain concurrency one. Unclassified tools remain sequential even when concurrency four is requested.
- A result checkpoint failure interrupts an in-flight read and prevents later mutation and model execution.
- Cancellation during a blocked read batch interrupts both cooperative reads and prevents later tools and model execution.
- Maximum iteration termination executes no tools; a failed assistant checkpoint starts no reads.
- Cancellation returns while an intentionally uncooperative extension remains held. The test releases and joins that extension afterward, demonstrating bounded coordinator cleanup without claiming a hard tool kill.

Coordination uses latches with bounded timeouts. The sequential negative case uses a 100 ms bounded latch wait while the first call is deliberately held; there are no product latency or speed assertions. All created tool threads are released or interrupted by test cleanup.

## Verification

Ran `python harness-core\target\parallel-read-acceptance\verify.py` with JDK 21. It compiled current core production sources and the new test into a private target directory using existing Surefire dependency classpaths, then invoked all eight JUnit test methods. Result: **8 passed**. The generated helper is not a deliverable.

No Maven or external network calls were made. The lead should run the serialized reactor to verify these tests with CLI and benchmark integration. No defect was reproduced against the current core implementation by this suite.

# Parallel-read audit

Lead resolution: added `resultCallbacksCancelBeforeFollowingMutationBarrier` covering both callbacks after one/two reads. Full reactor passed 2026-10-14 11:35:44 Asia/Shanghai. The original finding below is retained as review history.

## Result

No additional concrete production defect was established in this read-only audit. The current scheduler has no acceptance test for cancellation raised by a tool progress callback between a completed safe-read batch and the next unsafe tool. `executeReadBatch` publishes each result through `onCheckpoint` and `onToolResult`, then checks the cancellation supplier at the end of the batch. A callback can set the cancellation flag in `onToolResult` for the last read; the implementation checks it before entering the mutation barrier, but this boundary is currently untested.

This is a regression-test opportunity, not a reproduced correctness failure. Tool callbacks are user supplied and can change the cancellation state; losing the boundary checks could start a write or command after cancellation.

## Reproduction/test recommendation

Add a deterministic latch-free test with calls `[safe_read, mutate]` and `maxParallelReads=2`. The safe read returns normally. In `AgentListener.onToolResult` for that read, set an `AtomicBoolean` cancellation flag. The mutation tool increments an `AtomicInteger` and should never run. Assert `AgentResult.Status.CANCELLED`, one model request, zero mutations, one tool result in the transcript, and no mutation `onToolStart` callback. Repeat with two safe reads in the same batch and set the flag on the second (last) result to cover ordered result publication.

The same test should assert that a cancellation set by `onCheckpoint` after the last read result also prevents the barrier. Use no sleeps or elapsed-time thresholds. Keep the test in the existing parallel-read acceptance suite; no production change is proposed by this audit.

## Scope and evidence

Read-only audit of `harness-core/src/main/java/dev/codeharness/core/agent/CodeAgent.java` and the eight-test `ParallelReadsTest` suite. The existing implementation performs the expected cancellation check when `executeReadBatch` returns, and the current suite covers cancellation while reads are blocked, checkpoint failure and uncooperative cleanup. The gap is the callback-to-barrier boundary above. No Maven, network or live model call was used.

# Bounded parallel read benchmark

Measured locally on Windows 11 / Java 21.0.10: serial p50/p95 741.024/744.4713 ms; four-read p50/p95 184.2746/185.5673 ms. All ten measured samples passed output/barrier checks; observed peak reads were one versus four. Each sample used two scripted model requests with the same 3,255 serialized request bytes. Raw evidence: [parallel-reads-v1.json](benchmarks/parallel-reads-v1.json). This is approximately 4.02x lower elapsed time in this delayed mock workload only; real disk/provider/coding speed and token savings were not measured.

`dev.codeharness.cli.bench.ToolExecutionBenchmark` runs the real `CodeAgent` with two scripted model responses and two local fixture tools. Four reads each wait 80 ms, an unsafe mutation increments state, then four further reads each wait 80 ms. It compares read concurrency limits one and four, with one warmup each and five fresh-state measured samples each. Execution order alternates by sample. No network, credentials, real disk workload or model service is used.

The JSON report records nearest-rank p50/p95 `CodeAgent.run` elapsed milliseconds, each sample's observed maximum active reads and overlap, final state, read completion count, model request count, per-request message/schema counts and serialized request bytes. Timing includes the modeled waits. Initialization outside `CodeAgent.run`, JSON report generation and process startup are excluded. Small-sample p95 is the maximum observed sample; it is not a production tail-latency estimate.

Correctness checks run independently of timing: exact ordered result IDs/names/contents, all pre-mutation reads observe zero, all post-mutation reads observe one, no read overlaps the mutation, exactly eight reads complete, exactly two requests occur and final state is one. The two modes must produce equivalent request counts and serialized payload sizes. A concurrency cap violation fails the benchmark. Actual overlap is reported rather than inferred from elapsed time; absence of overlap does not fabricate a speed claim.

After a successful reactor build:

```shell
java -cp harness-cli/target/harness-cli-0.1.0-SNAPSHOT-all.jar dev.codeharness.cli.bench.ToolExecutionBenchmark
```

This models a workload where independent reads wait on latency. Any observed speed difference applies only to that fixture on the measured host. It does not demonstrate faster real coding, disk reads, provider generation, or lower token costs. The focused test checks correctness and report shape with a shorter delay without asserting a speed threshold. The lead owns serialized Maven verification and archiving actual benchmark results; this handoff itself makes no test-pass claim.

# Parallel read CLI handoff

`--parallel-reads` and trusted/explicit `agent.parallel-reads` YAML select 1 through 8 concurrent safe reads, defaulting to 1. ## Shared core contract, lead owned

Tool adds `default boolean isParallelSafeRead() { return false; }`. True asserts read-only, thread-safe concurrent reads and cooperative interruption. Unknown/custom/MCP tools default false. AgentRunOptions adds seventh component `int maxParallelReads`, validates 1..8. Keep six-argument constructor defaulting to 1, and defaults() still 1. Core runs consecutive safe-read calls in bounded batches of at most maxParallelReads, maintaining call order in results/checkpoints. Unsafe tools are sequential barriers: no read overlaps mutation/command/unknown tools. Durable assistant checkpoint precedes starts; result checkpoints happen on coordinator thread in call order. Checkpoint failure/cancellation interrupts in-flight reads and runs no later tools. Cancellation flag is polled during waits. Virtual executor cleanup must not block forever on uncooperative extensions; no hard tool-kill guarantee.

Implement deterministic latch-based tests against proposed shared contract: concurrent safe reads overlap and never exceed cap; unsafe mutation barrier waits for all prior reads and later reads observe mutation; results/checkpoints follow call order despite reversed completion; default options and unclassified tools remain serial; checkpoint failure prevents later mutation; cancellation during wait interrupts reads and prevents later tools/model; max iteration does not execute calls. # Provider finish-marker repair

## Result

OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages now require a nonblank textual completion marker. Missing, null, blank, whitespace-only and nontext markers fail with a sanitized `ProviderException` before a response reaches the agent. Unknown textual markers continue to fail. This closes the malformed response path documented in `PROVIDER_FOLLOWUP.md`, which previously inferred a successful completion and could execute supplied mutation calls.

## Owned changes

- `harness-providers/src/main/java/dev/codeharness/providers/OpenAiCompatibleProvider.java`: require an explicit valid `finish_reason` rather than defaulting to `stop`.
- `harness-providers/src/main/java/dev/codeharness/providers/AnthropicProvider.java`: require an explicit valid `stop_reason` rather than defaulting to `end_turn`.
- `harness-providers/src/test/java/dev/codeharness/providers/ProviderFinishStateTest.java`: four localhost acceptance tests covering both protocols, OpenAI aliases, Azure inheritance and actual `CodeAgent` mutation prevention.

Explicit supported marker mappings remain intact. Existing compatibility behavior for explicit STOP/end_turn responses containing calls remains intact. No core or CLI sources were changed.

## Evidence

Ran `python harness-providers\target\finish-state-acceptance\verify.py` using JDK 21 and existing Surefire dependency classpaths. The helper compiled only the edited providers and new test into a private target directory, then invoked the four test methods. Result: **4 tests passed**.

The tests exercise missing, null, blank, whitespace, number, object, array, boolean and unknown text markers with and without tool calls. A recording `write_file` integration verifies missing/null responses yield FAILED, execute zero mutations and append no tool-result transcript entries. OpenAI, generic compatible, Ollama and Azure aliases all reject a missing marker. Error messages omit arbitrary marker text and attach no raw response cause.

All traffic was localhost. No Maven invocation or live model call was made. Lead should run the serialized reactor to validate these changes with current core/CLI edits and all existing fixtures. The private helper is generated under target and is not a deliverable.

Final lead acceptance: serialized `mvn -B verify` passed at 2026-10-14 10:45:22 Asia/Shanghai, including all 45 provider tests and the complete core/CLI reactor. # Provider review

Status: provider repair, LangChain4j streaming, Responses acceptance, and Gemini function-call metadata follow-ups verified locally. The original audit below is historical; current coverage and validation are recorded at the end.

Latest continuation: native Chat Completions streaming is now implemented and verified for the OpenAI/OpenAI-compatible/Ollama/Azure adapter path. Earlier statements below that all native adapters are synchronous are historical. See [native streaming](NATIVE_STREAMING.md) for current protocol bounds and evidence. Full reactor on 2026-10-14 12:00:05 Asia/Shanghai passed 212 tests with six platform skips; seven packaged smokes passed. Real-vendor/Linux validation remains open.

## Confirmed from source

1. GeminiProvider.encode serializes tool results using parseObject(message.content()). Normal workspace tools return plain text. Any read/search/run tool result that is not JSON fails before the second model request. JSON arrays/scalars are silently discarded. Wrap non-object content in an output/result object.
2. AbstractHttpChatModel follows redirects while attaching authorization headers and x-api-key. Disable automatic redirects or explicitly restrict credentials and redirects to same origin; test with two localhost servers.
3. OpenAI and Anthropic decode treat missing response envelopes, content-filter/refusal errors, and malformed finish reasons as STOP. The agent can mark an empty/broken provider response as success. Add strict response validation and explicit FinishReason.CONTENT_FILTER handling.
4. Custom config.headers() are added with builder.header after protocolHeaders(), so Authorization / x-api-key overrides produce duplicate values. Combine keys case-insensitively or use setHeader.
5. ProviderConfig.toString() includes baseUri verbatim; URL query credentials and userinfo leak. Reject userinfo and either reject query or safely redact endpoint formatting.
6. All provider errors retain raw exceptions as causes; redacting only top-level exception text does not prevent credentials appearing in stack traces.
7. Anthropic token usage counts input_tokens but omits cache_read_input_tokens and cache_creation_input_tokens from total input count. This differs from OpenAI/Gemini total input semantics and under-reports cached input consumption.
8. Gemini thought signatures/opaque provider tool metadata are not retained in core ToolCall/ChatMessage. Modern models may reject a follow-up tool response when the required signature is absent. This needs a core SPI change or an honest supported-model limitation.
9. OpenAI sends max_tokens unconditionally; newer reasoning models require max_completion_tokens. Provide endpoint-specific output-limit support/config rather than silently promising all models.
10. LangChain4j dependencies are declared but no adapter uses them, including Bedrock. Current registry supports openai, openai-compatible, ollama, anthropic, gemini, azure-openai; do not advertise native Bedrock.

## Build observations

exec_command using cmd.exe/login=false works; PowerShell startup fails with CET support error. Maven path: D:\software\apache-maven-3.9.14\bin\mvn.cmd. Single-module test needs -am because core is not installed. Reactor provider tests currently stop at concurrent CodeAgent.java compilation referencing nonexistent FinishReason.CONTENT_FILTER (line 82). This appears to be in-progress lead/core work.

## Repair pass completed

Fixed findings 1–7 and 9 in harness-providers and expanded ProviderAdapterTest from 6 to 16 tests. Added grouped parallel tool result serialization for Anthropic and Gemini. All 16 tests pass with the in-process Surefire runner:

    mvn -pl harness-providers -am test -Dtest=ProviderAdapterTest -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false -DforkCount=0

Default forked Surefire failed ClassNotFoundException despite compiled test classes; the in-process test runner succeeds. Root build settings have not been changed by this worker. Items 8 and 10 remain broader compatibility/build architecture work. Native OpenAI and Azure now use max_completion_tokens; generic compatible endpoints and Ollama retain max_tokens.

## LangChain4j implementation completed

The registry now includes `langchain4j-openai`, a genuine LangChain4j 1.22.0 adapter using inspected `OpenAiChatModel` and JDK HTTP APIs. It maps system/user/assistant/tool-result messages, nested object and array schemas, tool calls, finish reasons, and input/output/cache usage. Redirects are disabled and SDK exception details are sanitized. The provider module retains the used OpenAI and JDK transport LangChain4j dependencies; unused Anthropic/Gemini/Azure/Bedrock artifacts were removed. Native HTTP adapters remain available. Native Bedrock support is not implemented.

## Gemini function-call metadata completed

`ToolCall` now has immutable `Map<String,String> providerMetadata`, copied on construction. The original three-argument constructor remains available and produces an empty map. Jackson reads older records lacking `providerMetadata`; a missing or null map becomes empty. A serialization round-trip test verifies metadata survives unchanged. The canonical record constructor has changed, so external SPI extensions should be recompiled.

The native Gemini adapter preserves returned `functionCall.id` as the core call ID and under `gemini.functionCallId` metadata. The metadata distinguishes provider IDs from locally generated correlation IDs. A `thoughtSignature` attached to a function-call part is retained verbatim under `gemini.thoughtSignature` and replayed on its matching function-call part. Matching `functionResponse` parts include the returned wire ID. Signatures and wire IDs are never fabricated when absent; only an internal correlation ID is generated.

Two-turn localhost contract tests cover parallel calls of the same tool, distinct wire IDs, a signature on only one call, exact signature replay, matching result IDs, and missing signatures/IDs. Function arguments must be JSON objects. Missing and unknown finish reasons fail. Text marked `thought: true` is excluded from visible assistant text.

This initial function-only limitation was superseded by the message metadata continuation below. Multimodal and universal model compatibility remain unverified/unsupported.

## Current validation

Focused provider validation passed on 2026-10-11 with the default forked Surefire runner:

```text
mvn -B -pl harness-providers -am test -Dtest=ProviderAdapterTest,LangChain4jOpenAiProviderTest,GeminiMetadataTest -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false
```

27 tests passed: 16 native adapter tests, 7 LangChain4j tests, and 4 Gemini metadata tests. All HTTP tests use local mock servers; no real provider API calls were made. Core and CLI persistence/integration validation is coordinated by the lead. The earlier temporary forked runner failure no longer reproduces.

## Final acceptance on 2026-10-14

The interrupted streaming implementation had orphan exception handlers and a missing redaction helper. These were repaired without retaining SDK exception causes. The LangChain4j adapter's streaming overload is exercised by seven local SSE tests: early text before completion, fragmented function arguments, cached usage, unfinished stream rejection, observer isolation, timeout, HTTP error redaction and interruption. Multiple assertions share tests. Native adapters remain synchronous. A packaged streaming smoke test additionally verifies early stdout, no repeated final answer and parseable JSON with the real shaded jar.

`openai-responses` uses `/responses`, `store:false`, `max_output_tokens` and `reasoning.encrypted_content`. Seven local contract tests verify ordered encrypted reasoning/message/function replay across two turns, parallel call/result IDs, usage, null errors, incomplete/refused responses, malformed/unsupported output, tampered replay rejection before HTTP, and provider-neutral history. The raw output array is stored on the first tool call and replayed after ID/name/argument validation. Incomplete/refused responses never expose calls for execution.

Responses support is limited to text and local function tools. Built-in tools, multimodal output, streaming Responses, and reasoning-only final answers are unsupported. Reasoning requires encrypted content. The initial final-turn carrier limitation was closed by the message metadata continuation below. Sessions may contain opaque reasoning data and must be kept private.

Final `mvn -B verify` with default forked Surefire passed: 30 core, 41 provider and 43 CLI tests discovered; 108 passed and six Windows capability skips, with no failures/errors. Only Windows was executed locally; the Ubuntu/Windows CI matrix is configured but was not run remotely. No paid or live provider calls were used.

## Message metadata continuation, 2026-10-14 11:05 Asia/Shanghai

`ChatMessage` and `ChatResponse` now carry immutable provider metadata. Prior constructor overloads and missing/null old-session maps remain supported; external SPI extensions must be recompiled because the canonical record signatures changed. The loop checkpoints response metadata, both accounting strategies include it, and compaction preserves the visible projection of retained replay-bearing messages.

Responses stores ordered supported output on the message for tool and final turns, with legacy first-call fallback. Gemini stores ordered supported parts, including signed thought/text and interleaved functions; thought text stays hidden. Both validate replay consistency before HTTP and reject ambiguous replay JSON. This verifies structural replay, not cryptographic authenticity or all vendor/model combinations. See [Responses details](RESPONSES_CONTINUITY.md) and [Gemini details](GEMINI_CONTINUITY.md).

Combined reactor: 38 core + 57 provider + 85 CLI = 180 discovered, 174 passed, six platform skips, zero failures/errors. All five actual-jar smoke scripts passed. The new `smoke_message_metadata.py` uses four localhost requests across separate CLI processes and checks exact final-turn persistence/replay plus tampering rejected before HTTP. Live vendor and Linux execution remain unverified.

# 厂商适配器评审

状态：厂商修复、LangChain4j 流式输出、Responses 验收和 Gemini 函数调用元数据后续工作已在本地验证。以下原始审计为历史记录；当前覆盖与验证记录在末尾。

最近续接：OpenAI/OpenAI-compatible/Ollama/Azure 适配器路径现在已实现并验证原生 Chat Completions 流式输出。下文“全部原生适配器同步”的说法是历史状态。当前协议上限和证据见[原生流式输出](NATIVE_STREAMING.md)。2026-10-14 12:00:05 Asia/Shanghai 的完整 reactor 通过 212 项测试、六项平台跳过；七个打包冒烟测试通过。此历史检查时真实厂商/Linux 验证仍待完成；后续 CodeGo 实测另见 CODEGO_EVALUATION.md。

## 从源码确认的问题

1. GeminiProvider.encode 使用 parseObject(message.content()) 序列化工具结果。普通工作区工具返回纯文本。任何不是 JSON 的 read/search/run 结果都会在第二次模型请求前失败。JSON 数组/标量被静默丢弃。应把非对象内容包装到 output/result 对象中。
2. AbstractHttpChatModel 携带 authorization 请求头和 x-api-key 时仍跟随重定向。应禁止自动重定向，或明确限制凭据和重定向为同源；用两个 localhost 服务测试。
3. OpenAI 和 Anthropic 解码将缺失响应包、内容过滤/拒答错误和错误 finish reason 当作 STOP。智能体可能把空/损坏厂商响应标记为成功。应增加严格响应验证并显式处理 FinishReason.CONTENT_FILTER。
4. 自定义 config.headers() 在 protocolHeaders() 后通过 builder.header 添加，因此 Authorization / x-api-key 覆盖会产生重复值。应按大小写不敏感方式合并键，或使用 setHeader。
5. ProviderConfig.toString() 原样包含 baseUri，URL 查询凭据和 userinfo 会泄露。应拒绝 userinfo，并拒绝 query 或安全脱敏端点格式。
6. 全部厂商错误保留原始异常为 cause；仅对顶层异常文本脱敏不能阻止密钥出现在堆栈中。
7. Anthropic 用量统计包含 input_tokens，但总输入省略 cache_read_input_tokens 和 cache_creation_input_tokens。它与 OpenAI/Gemini 总输入语义不同，会低报缓存输入消耗。
8. 核心 ToolCall/ChatMessage 不保留 Gemini thought signature/不透明厂商工具元数据。现代模型可能因缺失必需签名而拒绝后续工具响应。需要改核心 SPI，或如实声明受支持模型限制。
9. OpenAI 无条件发送 max_tokens；较新的推理模型要求 max_completion_tokens。应按端点支持/配置输出上限，不应静默承诺全部模型可用。
10. 声明了 LangChain4j 依赖，但没有适配器使用它，包括 Bedrock。当时注册表仅支持 openai、openai-compatible、ollama、anthropic、gemini、azure-openai；不能宣称原生 Bedrock。

## 构建观察

exec_command 使用 cmd.exe/login=false 可运行；PowerShell 启动因 CET 支持错误失败。Maven 路径：D:\software\apache-maven-3.9.14\bin\mvn.cmd。单模块测试需要 -am，因为 core 尚未安装。当时 reactor 厂商测试因并发中的 CodeAgent.java 引用不存在的 FinishReason.CONTENT_FILTER（第 82 行）而停止，似乎是负责人/核心成员正在进行的工作。

## 修复轮次完成

在 harness-providers 中修复问题 1–7 和 9，把 ProviderAdapterTest 从 6 项扩展为 16 项。增加 Anthropic 和 Gemini 的分组并行工具结果序列化。16 项测试在进程内 Surefire 运行器中全部通过：

    mvn -pl harness-providers -am test -Dtest=ProviderAdapterTest -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false -DforkCount=0

默认 forked Surefire 即使已编译测试类仍发生 ClassNotFoundException；进程内运行器成功。该成员没有修改根构建设置。问题 8 和 10 仍属于更广泛兼容性/构建架构工作。原生 OpenAI 和 Azure 现在使用 max_completion_tokens；通用兼容端点和 Ollama 保留 max_tokens。

## LangChain4j 实现完成

注册表现在包含 `langchain4j-openai`，使用检查过的 `OpenAiChatModel` 和 JDK HTTP API 实现真正的 LangChain4j 1.22.0 适配器。它映射 system/user/assistant/tool-result 消息、嵌套对象和数组 schema、工具调用、finish reason，以及输入/输出/缓存用量。禁止重定向，SDK 异常细节脱敏。厂商模块保留实际使用的 OpenAI 和 JDK 传输 LangChain4j 依赖；未使用的 Anthropic/Gemini/Azure/Bedrock 产物被移除。原生 HTTP 适配器仍可用。未实现原生 Bedrock 支持。

## Gemini 函数调用元数据完成

`ToolCall` 现在包含不可变 `Map<String,String> providerMetadata`，构造时复制。原有三参数构造器仍可用，并产生空 map。Jackson 可读取缺少 `providerMetadata` 的旧记录；缺失或 null map 转为空。序列化往返测试验证元数据不变。记录规范构造器改变，外部 SPI 扩展应重新编译。

原生 Gemini 适配器把返回的 `functionCall.id` 保留为核心调用 ID，并存入 `gemini.functionCallId` 元数据，以区分厂商 ID 和本地生成的关联 ID。函数调用 part 上的 `thoughtSignature` 原样保留到 `gemini.thoughtSignature`，并在对应函数调用 part 上回放。匹配的 `functionResponse` parts 包含返回的传输 ID。签名和传输 ID 缺失时绝不伪造；只生成内部关联 ID。

两轮 localhost 契约测试覆盖同一工具并行调用、不同传输 ID、只有一个调用带签名、精确签名回放、匹配结果 ID，以及缺失签名/ID。函数参数必须为 JSON 对象。缺失和未知 finish reason 会失败。标记 `thought: true` 的文本不进入可见助手文本。

最初仅支持函数的限制已由下文消息元数据续接覆盖。多模态和通用模型兼容性仍未验证/不受支持。

## 当时的验证

2026-10-11，针对性厂商验证在默认 forked Surefire 运行器中通过：

```text
mvn -B -pl harness-providers -am test -Dtest=ProviderAdapterTest,LangChain4jOpenAiProviderTest,GeminiMetadataTest -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false
```

27 项测试通过：16 项原生适配器、7 项 LangChain4j、4 项 Gemini 元数据。所有 HTTP 测试使用本地模拟服务，未调用真实厂商 API。核心和 CLI 持久化/集成验证由负责人协调。早期临时 forked 运行器失败已不能复现。

## 2026-10-14 历史最终验收

中断的流式实现留下孤立异常处理器和缺失的脱敏辅助方法，已修复，并且没有保留 SDK 异常 cause。LangChain4j 适配器的流式重载由七项本地 SSE 测试验证：完成前提前文本、分片函数参数、缓存用量、未结束流拒绝、观察者隔离、超时、HTTP 错误脱敏和中断；多个断言共用测试。当时原生适配器仍同步执行。打包流式冒烟测试还用真实 shaded jar 验证提前 stdout、最终答案不重复和可解析 JSON。

`openai-responses` 使用 `/responses`、`store:false`、`max_output_tokens` 和 `reasoning.encrypted_content`。七项本地契约测试验证两轮间有序的加密推理/消息/函数回放、并行调用/结果 ID、用量、null 错误、不完整/拒答响应、格式错误/不支持输出、HTTP 前篡改回放拒绝，以及厂商中立历史。原始输出数组保存在首个工具调用上，经过 ID/名称/参数验证后回放。不完整/拒答响应绝不暴露可执行调用。

Responses 支持仅限文本和本地函数工具。不支持内置工具、多模态输出、流式 Responses 和仅推理的最终答案。推理要求加密内容。最初最终轮次载体的限制已由下文消息元数据续接关闭。会话可能包含不透明推理数据，必须保持私密。

当时最终 `mvn -B verify` 使用默认 forked Surefire 通过：发现 30 项 core、41 项 provider、43 项 CLI；108 项通过、六项 Windows 能力跳过，无失败/错误。仅在 Windows 本地执行；Ubuntu/Windows CI 矩阵已配置，但未远程运行。未使用付费或真实厂商调用。

## 消息元数据续接，2026-10-14 11:05 Asia/Shanghai

`ChatMessage` 和 `ChatResponse` 现在携带不可变厂商元数据。既有构造器重载和旧会话缺失/null map 仍受支持；规范记录签名改变，外部 SPI 扩展必须重新编译。循环将响应元数据写入检查点，两种统计策略都包含它，压缩保留已留存且含回放证据的消息可见投影。

Responses 在工具轮次和最终轮次的消息上保存有序的受支持输出，兼容旧式首调用回退。Gemini 保存有序的受支持 parts，包括签名 thought/text 和交错函数；thought 文本保持隐藏。两者在 HTTP 前验证回放一致性，并拒绝存在歧义的回放 JSON。这验证结构回放，不验证加密真实性或全部厂商/模型组合。详见 [Responses 说明](RESPONSES_CONTINUITY.md)和 [Gemini 说明](GEMINI_CONTINUITY.md)。

组合 reactor：38 core + 57 provider + 85 CLI = 180 项发现、174 项通过、六项平台跳过、零失败/错误。五个实际 jar 冒烟脚本全部通过。新增 `smoke_message_metadata.py` 跨独立 CLI 进程发送四个 localhost 请求，检查精确最终轮次持久化/回放和 HTTP 前篡改拒绝。该历史检查时真实厂商和 Linux 执行仍未验证。

# Session recovery acceptance handoff

## Changes

`SessionStore.validate` now calls the shared `ToolHistory.validate(transcript, true)` on both save and load. Pending and partial results remain valid checkpoints. Duplicate calls, duplicate/orphan/unmatched results and mismatched tool names fail with a fixed `IOException("Invalid session tool history")` without a nested exception exposing persisted evidence. Validation happens before acquiring a save lease or creating/replacing a checkpoint.

`SessionStoreTest` adds two cases: five malformed histories are rejected both through save and externally written valid JSON; failed saves preserve existing bytes and leave no temporary files. Pending and partially completed checkpoints round-trip unchanged.

`SessionRecoveryProcessTest` starts a separate Java subprocess using a local mock model and actual `CodeAgent`/`SessionStore` checkpoints. Its tool writes a mutation marker and a ready barrier, then blocks before returning a tool result while holding the session lease. The parent verifies a complete pending checkpoint and exactly one mutation, forcibly terminates the child, waits for its exit, reloads identical committed bytes, reacquires the released lease and resumes. The model sees an uncertain-effect result; the mutation tool is not replayed. The completed checkpoint retains provider/model metadata and the uncertain result. No network or paid model calls are involved.

The child is killed at a controlled process interruption boundary, not a power-loss boundary. This test does not claim fsync durability or Windows process-tree containment.

The crash fixture now also returns a non-empty opaque `ToolCall.providerMetadata` map containing a Gemini thought signature and a second opaque value with escape/newline characters. Exact map equality is asserted in the initial pending checkpoint, reloaded checkpoint after process death, resumed model request and completed persisted transcript. These assertions verify opaque tool metadata separately from the session's provider/model labels; no live provider serialization claim is made by this local recovery test.

## Verification

No Maven invocation was started by this agent. Direct Java 21 compilation of `ToolHistory`, `SessionStore` and the two CLI test classes succeeded using the existing shaded artifact and dependency paths from the project-local Surefire report. Compilation output is isolated under `harness-cli/target/mcp-check`. The lead should run `SessionStoreTest,SessionRecoveryProcessTest` with the newly compiled core, then serialized reactor verification. The new process test uses the test JVM's `java.class.path`, matching existing MCP subprocess fixtures.

Owned source changes: `SessionStore.java`, `SessionStoreTest.java`, new `SessionRecoveryProcessTest.java`. Core sources/tests remain lead-owned and were not edited. Other agents' edits are preserved.

Final lead acceptance: serialized `mvn -B verify` passed at 2026-10-14 10:45:22 Asia/Shanghai, including all 15 SessionStore tests (two platform skips), the subprocess-death test and eight core recovery tests. The packaged CLI/resume smoke also passed on the rebuilt artifact. Earlier direct-compilation evidence above is the worker handoff, not the final acceptance.

`SessionRecoveryProcessTest` 启动独立 Java 子进程，使用本地模拟模型及真实 `CodeAgent`/`SessionStore` 检查点。工具写入修改标记和就绪屏障，持有会话租约并在返回工具结果前阻塞。父进程验证完整待执行检查点和恰好一次修改，强制终止子进程，等待退出，重新加载相同的已提交字节，重新获取释放的租约并恢复。模型看到效果不确定结果，修改工具不重放。完成检查点保留厂商/模型元数据及不确定结果。不涉及网络或付费模型调用。

# Recovery follow-up evidence

## MCP fixture readiness publication repair

The final reactor exposed a test-fixture publication race: the interruption test observed `pid.txt` existing between file creation and completion of `Files.writeString`, cancelled the child, then parsed an empty PID. The fixture now writes a complete unique temporary PID file and atomically replaces the PID path in the same directory. Observing the final path is therefore a readiness barrier with complete content. `config` clears an earlier PID before every launch, and the interruption branch retains its explicit deletion before reusing the same configuration. This also prevents earlier stopped processes from satisfying later launch-readiness checks.

Existing timeout and direct-server termination assertions are unchanged; no deadline was increased and no production source was modified for this fixture repair. Trace checks occur after completed JSON-RPC request/response handling, while the interrupted fixture publishes PID before blocking, so the remaining readiness assumptions do not parse a concurrently created empty file. No Maven run was started; lead verification remains serialized.

## MCP timeout cleanup repair

The serialized Surefire report reproduced a production deadline failure in `McpToolsTest.timeoutAndInterruptionStopTheSubprocess`: the five-second outer bound expired while the MCP request had already reached its one-second timeout. The stack was `StdioMcpClient.close` -> `Process.descendants` -> `ProcessHandleImpl.getProcessPids0`. Direct process termination was after descendant enumeration, so a native stall left the server alive and its workspace locked.

`StdioMcpClient.stopProcess` now schedules best-effort descendant enumeration on a daemon platform thread and calls `destroyForcibly` on the configured direct process without waiting for that discovery. Pipe closure also runs on a separate daemon thread because it can wait for a blocked stdin-write monitor. Neither native tree discovery nor pipe cleanup is joined by request/close. Enumeration considers at most 1,024 descendant handles. Process-tree cleanup remains best effort: terminating the direct process can orphan descendants before discovery completes, and native discovery may itself remain stalled. This is not an OS process sandbox; guaranteed Windows tree termination would require a job-object implementation, which is outside this repair.

The test deadline was not increased. Added `directTerminationDoesNotWaitForStalledNativeDescendantDiscovery`, which supplies a process whose descendant enumeration blocks on a latch, verifies cleanup returns within 500 ms and directly terminates the process while discovery remains blocked, then releases the daemon for cleanup. Existing fixture timeout/interruption/CLI lifecycle tests still verify actual direct-server termination.

No Maven run was started by this agent. Lead verification should rerun `McpToolsTest,McpCliTest` serially before the reactor. Changed production source: only `cli/mcp/StdioMcpClient.java`; changed test source: only `cli/mcp/McpToolsTest.java`.

## Read-only checkpoint audit

Historical findings below were implemented in this continuation: core `ToolHistory` validates provider call IDs before checkpoint/dispatch and validates resume evidence before repair; `SessionStore` validates save/load history while allowing pending results. A real process-death test was added as described in [RECOVERY_ACCEPTANCE.md](RECOVERY_ACCEPTANCE.md). Final serialized reactor acceptance passed at 2026-10-14 10:45:22 Asia/Shanghai, including all seven MCP tests and two MCP CLI tests. The packaged MCP smoke passed on the rebuilt jar. The findings below describe the pre-repair behavior.

The current checkpoint path correctly saves the assistant call record before tool effects, stops tool dispatch on checkpoint failure, saves individual completed results, and substitutes uncertain-effect results on resume instead of automatically replaying calls. Atomic replacement, size limits, abandoned-temp isolation and locks have focused tests. The documentation correctly declines fsync/power-loss guarantees.

At audit time, a correctness gap allowed duplicate call IDs from a provider response. `ChatResponse` and `ChatMessage` accepted duplicate IDs within an assistant turn. Pre-repair `CodeAgent` checkpointed that response and dispatched each requested call before its next compaction validated pairing. A response containing two `ToolCall("same", "edit", "{}")` entries could invoke the mutating tool twice; only the next iteration failed with unmatched/duplicate call/results. It also persisted a checkpoint that could not be safely paired. The new pre-dispatch validation and regression test close this path.

Recommended reproduction/test: use a local `ChatModel` returning those two calls on its first turn and an `edit` tool incrementing an `AtomicInteger`. Capture checkpoints. With current code, executions become two before the second iteration fails. Expected safe behavior is `FAILED`, zero tool executions, no malformed assistant-call checkpoint, and a descriptive duplicate-ID error. Validate the response call set before checkpointing or dispatch. No core source was modified by this audit.

The audit also found silent evidence loss in resume repair: `repairInterruptedTools` indexed consecutive tool results using `results.put(id, message)`, overwriting duplicate IDs, and emitted only IDs present in the assistant calls, discarding unmatched results. Pre-repair `SessionStore` validated checkpoint identity/metadata without rejecting malformed call/result relationships. A loaded transcript with one assistant call followed by two results for that ID could resume using only the last result and overwrite the checkpoint before requesting the provider. Shared history validation now rejects that evidence before repair/save/load; regression tests verify no model/checkpoint/tool effects and unchanged checkpoint bytes. Genuinely missing results still receive uncertain-effect placeholders.

The audit identified a missing real crash-boundary integration test. The added child runner saves a pending call, mutates a marker, signals a barrier and blocks; the parent terminates it, reloads the checkpoint and resumes with a mock model. Passing assertions verify one side effect, no tool replay, an unknown-effect result, exact opaque tool metadata preservation, released lock and complete persisted JSON. This verifies recovery across process death; it does not establish power-loss durability.

# 恢复后续证据

## MCP 夹具就绪发布修复

最终 reactor 暴露测试夹具发布竞态：中断测试在文件创建与 `Files.writeString` 完成之间观察到 `pid.txt` 存在，取消子进程，随后解析了空 PID。夹具现先写完整唯一临时 PID 文件，再在相同目录原子替换 PID 路径。因此观察最终路径即是内容完整的就绪屏障。`config` 每次启动前删除旧 PID；中断分支再次使用相同配置前，也保留显式删除。这样也阻止早前已停止进程满足后续启动就绪检查。

现有超时和直接服务终止断言不变，未增加截止时间，也未为夹具修复改变生产源码。trace 检查在完整 JSON-RPC 请求/响应处理后执行；中断夹具先发布 PID 再阻塞，因此其余就绪假设不会解析并发创建的空文件。未启动 Maven，负责人继续串行验证。

## MCP 超时清理修复

串行 Surefire 报告复现 `McpToolsTest.timeoutAndInterruptionStopTheSubprocess` 的生产截止失败：MCP 请求已经达到一秒超时，外层五秒边界仍超时。调用栈为 `StdioMcpClient.close` -> `Process.descendants` -> `ProcessHandleImpl.getProcessPids0`。直接终止在后代枚举之后，原生调用卡住导致服务存活、工作区被锁。

`StdioMcpClient.stopProcess` 现将尽力的后代枚举调度到守护平台线程，同时对配置的直接进程调用 `destroyForcibly`，不等待发现。管道关闭也放独立守护线程，因为可能等待被阻塞的 stdin-write 监视器。请求/close 不 join 原生树发现或管道清理。枚举最多考虑 1,024 个后代句柄。进程树清理仍是尽力：直接进程终止可能在发现完成前留下孤立后代，原生发现自身也可能一直卡住。这不是操作系统进程沙箱；保证 Windows 树终止需要 job-object 实现，超出此次修复。

未提高测试截止时间。新增 `directTerminationDoesNotWaitForStalledNativeDescendantDiscovery`：提供后代枚举在 latch 阻塞的进程，验证清理在 500 ms 内返回，发现仍阻塞时直接终止进程，然后释放守护线程清理。已有夹具超时/中断/CLI 生命周期测试继续验证真实直接服务终止。

此成员未启动 Maven。负责人应先串行重跑 `McpToolsTest,McpCliTest`，再运行 reactor。生产源码只改 `cli/mcp/StdioMcpClient.java`；测试源码只改 `cli/mcp/McpToolsTest.java`。

检查点路径正确地在工具效果前保存助手调用记录，检查点失败时停止派发，保存各个完成结果，恢复时补入效果不确定结果而非自动重放调用。原子替换、大小限制、遗弃临时文件隔离和锁均有专门测试。文档正确说明不保证 fsync/断电持久性。

审计时，正确性缺口允许厂商响应中重复调用 ID。`ChatResponse`、`ChatMessage` 接受单助手回合重复 ID。修复前 `CodeAgent` 将响应写为检查点并执行每个请求调用，直到下次压缩才验证配对。响应中两个 `ToolCall("same", "edit", "{}")` 可两次调用修改工具，下一迭代才因不匹配/重复调用结果失败，同时持久化无法安全配对的检查点。新增派发前校验及回归测试关闭此路径。

Reference repairs and checks must stay outside the model workspace; live workspace preparation copies **only** the public source map and the prompt.

## Independent checker API

- `prepare_workspace(task, workspace)` writes public source snapshots as UTF-8/LF bytes, without copying checks/repairs.
- `verify_workspace(task, workspace, java, javac, timeout=20)` reads exact declared file bytes (no newline normalization), rejects missing/invalid UTF-8 snapshots, then verifies in fresh temporary isolation.
- `verify_sources(task, sources, java, javac, timeout=20)` accepts an exact declared snapshot map. Do not feed normalized `read_text()` values if claiming byte preservation; use `verify_workspace`.
- `run_controls(task, java, javac, timeout=20)` and the script main run verifier controls. Live runners must never call `apply_reference` on the model workspace.

The checker compiles exactly declared source snapshots plus private Check.java into fresh output, uses explicit empty classpath/sourcepath, `-proc:none`, `--release 21`, UTF-8 encoding and a fresh cwd. It runs Java only after compilation succeeds, with only fresh output on runtime classpath. Compile/assertion timeouts and IO failures report failed phase categories, without raw diagnostics. Exact unchanged file content and hashes are checked before compilation, so comment or newline-only changes fail preservation.

This isolates stale outputs/hidden checks and compiler discovery. It is not an OS sandbox: future model-generated Java can still execute with the current account's permissions. Included fixture/reference production code is deterministic and has no network, environment or process IO; checks use only assertions and the completion sentinel.

## Verified controls

Executed locally with installed JDK 21:

```text
python scripts/check_repository_fixtures.py --java D:\software\jdk-21.0.10\bin\java.exe --javac D:\software\jdk-21.0.10\bin\javac.exe
```

Result: **all 15 control variants matched expectation**. For each task the buggy snapshot failed assertions, the full reference repair passed, and every single omitted edited-file snapshot failed assertions. Checkout additionally rejected one changed-unchanged-file snapshot; ingestion rejected two. All three preservation controls failed in `source-invariants` before compiler execution. Reference edits match exactly once and alter exactly the four declared paths per task.

Verified fixture hash: `3a7cc1f7ddf1877e0ac9ee39ceebbbad5ad877d189eed9cb9b34bc52c9bca591`. Checker helper additions do not modify fixtures. No real coding run has been performed; these results establish the verifier controls and reference repairs, not model coding quality or token/latency performance.

# Independent repository runner audit

Reviewed `scripts/evaluate_repository.py`, `scripts/repository_fixtures.py`, and `scripts/check_repository_fixtures.py`. This audit owns documentation only. No Maven, external provider request, credential access, or source/configuration change was performed.

## Executed acceptance

Executed:

```text
python scripts/evaluate_repository.py --offline --variants paired --max-iterations 4 --timeout 60
```

The command exited 0. Report timestamp: `2026-10-14T09:22:29.337425+00:00`.

| Fixture | Variant / context estimate budget | Independent compile/assertions | Changed paths | Process / agent elapsed ms | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Checkout | baseline / 48000 | PASS | 4 | 1238.3615 / 163 | PASS |
| Checkout | compact / 12000 | PASS | 4 | 1247.5835 / 167 | PASS |
| Ingest | baseline / 48000 | PASS | 4 | 1215.8292 / 161 | PASS |
| Ingest | compact / 12000 | PASS | 4 | 1217.1519 / 145 | PASS |

Every run completed in two agent iterations and two localhost HTTP requests, with no fixture failures. Every run reported `requiredFilesChanged`, `unrelatedSourcesUnchanged`, and `workspaceAllowlist` true. Baseline and compact produced identical final source hashes within each fixture. Provider usage is absent for the localhost fixture.

Checkout contains nine public source files / 177 lines. Changed: `src/shop/CartLine.java`, `src/shop/DiscountPolicy.java`, `src/shop/PriceCalculator.java`, and `src/shop/ReceiptRenderer.java`. Protected `src/shop/BuildInfo.java` remained byte-identical.

Ingest contains ten public source files / 174 lines. Changed: `src/ingest/Tokenizer.java`, `src/ingest/RecordParser.java`, `src/ingest/BatchAccumulator.java`, and `src/ingest/ReportRenderer.java`. Protected `src/ingest/InputRow.java` and `src/ingest/BuildInfo.java` remained byte-identical.

Evidence identity:

```text
artifactSha256: 43d272eec8e2087f3e72bb5147cfdec5e2fba00be7614d7fef4dfe0b23d1e3a6
evaluatorSha256: d19542d0758465406dee3b99d4c06d19642801f9ae7b084c8f2fc15f4198c8c8
fixtureSha256: 3a7cc1f7ddf1877e0ac9ee39ceebbbad5ad877d189eed9cb9b34bc52c9bca591
```

These runs verify the packaged CLI repair/acceptance path using a deterministic server that supplies known repairs. They do not demonstrate live model reasoning, billed token savings, or a speed improvement. The elapsed values are individual observations, with no statistical comparison claim.

## Acceptance design review

- Public fixture sources are written as UTF-8 bytes, preserving canonical LF content. Initial/final comparisons use bytes, avoiding newline normalization when enforcing protected-file invariants.
- Hidden `Check.java` and reference edits are not copied into the model workspace. The offline server holds the known reference edits separately; live requests must produce their own patches.
- Verification copies declared snapshots into a fresh private temporary directory, compiles using Java 21 with explicit UTF-8, disables annotation processing, and uses empty compiler classpath/sourcepath. Agent-produced class files cannot satisfy checks. Assertions require process exit 0 and an exact `CHECKS_PASS` output line.
- The runner rejects source symlinks and canonical path redirection. Its workspace allowlist also rejects symlinks/redirection before considering runtime files. Missing, oversized, invalid UTF-8 Java input or failed compilation cannot pass the combined acceptance gate.
- Trusted provider configuration is outside the agent workspace. Commands and MCP tools are disabled. Offline requests use only localhost and remove their artificial credential variable; the fixture requires no Authorization header. Live mode requires explicit HTTPS URL, model, and configured credential variable.
- Compile/assertion failures report phase and exit code without exposing captured source/checker output. Timeout and invalid snapshot failures are sanitized. The final report applies recursive exact-credential redaction, including the agent error field.
- Fixture controls reviewed in source cover buggy input, known repairs, omission of each required changed file, and modification of each protected source. This audit did not rerun the separate controls command. The runner itself does not execute those negative controls.

## Source-derived gaps for the lead

1. **The runner does not enforce an exact Java source set across `.harness`.** `allowed_workspace()` exempts all regular files/directories beneath `.harness`; `source_snapshot()` and the independent compiler consider only declared sources. Consequently an extra `.harness/Extra.java` would be excluded from verification and would not make the allowlist fail. This is a source-derived gap, not an observed failing model run. If acceptance promises an exact workspace Java source set, reject additional `.java` files anywhere, including `.harness`, while retaining the intended session/log runtime files. Add a negative control for this case.
2. **The standalone fixture checker lacks the runner's symlink/canonical-path gate.** `verify_workspace()` enumerates `src/**/*.java` and reads declared paths without rejecting symlinks or parent redirection. Its generated controls use ordinary files, so current controls do not exercise this difference. Reuse the runner's canonical snapshot validation or add equivalent validation and a symlink/redirection negative control. The combined runner remains protected by its own checks.
3. **Protected bytes cover named unrelated sources only.** `requiredFilesChanged` requires inclusion of all four paths; it does not require changed paths to equal that set. Other declared helper sources may change unless listed in `unchanged_paths`. The observed runs changed exactly four files. Keep this distinction explicit in live reporting, or require exact equality if delivery claims that only those four files change.
4. **Live endpoint preflight is lexical.** The runner checks the `https://` prefix and rejects `?`, `#`, and `@`, but does not parse/validate a nonempty hostname itself. Java request construction should fail closed for malformed endpoints, but no such negative control was run in this audit. Prefer shared parsed-URL validation if the runner promises early endpoint diagnostics.

The private compiler directory is verification isolation, not a hostile-code execution sandbox, as the standalone checker explicitly documents. No broader isolation claim should be inferred from these results.

## Next acceptance work

The lead should decide the exact source-set/protected-file contract, add focused negative controls for any tightened contract, and retain the present offline evidence separately from credentialed live runs. Live results should include actual source hashes, changed paths, protected-byte evidence, independent checker results, and usage availability; this audit performs no live request.

1. **运行器未强制.harness下精确Java集合。** allowed_workspace豁免.harness下所有普通文件/目录；source_snapshot及独立编译器只考虑声明源码。因此额外.harness/Extra.java不验证也不使允许列表失败。这是源码缺口，不是观察的失败模型运行。若承诺精确工作区Java集合，应拒绝任何位置额外.java，包括.harness，同时保留会话/日志运行文件，并增加负对照。
2. **独立夹具检查器缺少运行器符号链接/规范路径门槛。** verify_workspace枚举src/**/*.java、读取声明路径，不拒绝符号链接/父重定向。生成对照是普通文件，未覆盖差异。应复用运行器规范快照验证，或等效验证及链接/重定向负对照。组合运行器仍由自身检查保护。
3. **保护字节只覆盖指定无关源码。** requiredFilesChanged只要求四路径包含，不要求修改集合等于它们。未列unchanged_paths的辅助源码可能修改。观察运行恰好改四文件。真实报告应明确，或若交付声称只改四文件则要求精确相等。
4. **真实端点预检只是字符检查。** 运行器检查https://前缀、拒绝?、#、@，但不解析/校验非空hostname。Java请求构建应拒绝非法端点，但本审计未跑此负对照。若承诺早期端点诊断，应采用共享解析URL验证。

私有编译目录是验证隔离，不是敌对代码执行沙箱，独立检查器明确如此。不应推断更广隔离。

## 下一验收工作

| [OpenAI function calling](https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/function-calling) | Explicit calls/results and iterative coding tools | Native Chat Completions adapter and bounded loop |
| [OpenAI Responses](https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/responses) | Stateless function output and encrypted reasoning replay | Text/functions adapter with two-turn local contracts |
| [Anthropic tool use](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/tool-use/overview) | Tool-use blocks and grouped results | Messages adapter with mock contract tests |
| [Gemini function calling](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling) | Function calls/results and provider metadata | generateContent adapter and retained call signatures |
| [LangGraph persistence](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/persistence) | Checkpoint state for resumable execution | Atomic local transcript checkpoints and uncertain-effect recovery |
| [Aider](https://aider.chat/docs/) | Focused code edits and compact repository context | Literal search, bounded reads and hash-guarded edits |
| [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/) | Extensible external tools | Research/backlog only; no MCP transport yet |

The initial engineering pass uses focused local search instead of an eager repository dump, stable schemas for cache opportunities, and bounded results. Future efficiency claims require comparable tasks, provider usage, quality checks and latency measurements; the current synthetic context estimate is only a regression fixture.

# OpenAI Responses message continuity

## Implemented behavior

Completed Responses text and function-tool turns now carry their ordered output array in `ChatResponse.providerMetadata["openai.responses.outputItems"]`. The updated core SPI persists this map on the assistant message. Final answers therefore retain encrypted reasoning for a later user follow-up, including through agent checkpoint/resume.

Replay preserves supported reasoning, assistant-message and function-call items, their order, IDs, message phase, annotations and other opaque fields. Reasoning remains hidden from visible text. Reasoning-only or blank-visible final output cannot complete a coding task. Reasoning items in completed replayable turns must contain encrypted content. Incomplete and refused responses return neither executable calls nor replayable metadata.

The adapter validates the raw replay projection against visible assistant text and all expected function IDs, names and JSON argument objects before HTTP. It rejects wrong-role metadata, malformed JSON, duplicate object keys, trailing JSON values, duplicate output IDs, duplicated later-call carriers, projection changes and conflicting dual copies. Function arguments use the same strict parsing for both raw replay and expected neutral calls. Equivalent JSON argument objects are allowed even when object-key order or whitespace differs.

Legacy sessions with output metadata on the first ToolCall still replay. If both message-level and legacy copies exist, both must validate and describe the same output array; the array is emitted once. New decode uses only the message-level carrier to avoid storing two copies.

Opaque values are preserved, not independently authenticated locally. Projection and copy validation detect inconsistent history; provider-side validation remains responsible for authenticating encrypted reasoning.

## Evidence

Ran `python harness-providers\target\responses-continuity-acceptance\verify.py` with JDK 21, compiling current core sources, the edited Responses provider and its JUnit test into a private target directory using existing Surefire dependency classpaths. Result: **13 tests passed**. The generated helper is not a deliverable.

Coverage includes:

- Ordered encrypted reasoning and parallel calls using the new message carrier.
- Final reasoning/text answer followed by a real CodeAgent checkpoint/resume and user follow-up, preserving phase and opaque annotations.
- Legacy first-call fallback and matching dual copies replayed once.
- Visible text/call changes, malformed and ambiguous JSON, missing encrypted reasoning, duplicate IDs and conflicting copies rejected before another HTTP request.
- Existing usage, incomplete/refusal, unsupported output and provider-neutral history contracts.

All requests were localhost. No Maven or live/paid model call was made. The lead must run the serialized reactor for combined verification.

## Changed deliverable files

- `harness-providers/src/main/java/dev/codeharness/providers/OpenAiResponsesProvider.java`
- `harness-providers/src/test/java/dev/codeharness/providers/OpenAiResponsesProviderTest.java`
- This document.

Reference supplied by the lead: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning (retrieved HTTP 200 on 2026-10-14). Stateless reasoning requires preserving ordered response output in history. The existing `store:false` and accepted encrypted-reasoning include remain unchanged.

# OpenAI Responses 消息连续性

## 已实现行为

完成的 Responses 文本与函数工具回合现在通过 `ChatResponse.providerMetadata["openai.responses.outputItems"]` 携带有序输出数组。更新后的核心 SPI 将映射持久化到助手消息。因此最终回答为后续用户追问保留加密推理，包括代理检查点/恢复路径。

回放保留受支持的 reasoning、assistant-message、function-call 项、顺序、ID、消息 phase、annotations 和其他不透明字段。推理不显示在可见文本中。只有推理或可见文本为空白的最终输出不能完成编码任务。已完成、可回放回合的 reasoning 项必须含加密内容。未完成和拒绝响应既不返回可执行调用，也不返回可回放元数据。

适配器在 HTTP 前，对照可见助手文本及全部预期函数 ID、名称、JSON 参数对象，校验原始回放投影。拒绝错误角色元数据、格式错误 JSON、重复对象键、尾随 JSON 值、重复输出 ID、后续调用重复载体、投影变化和冲突双副本。原始回放与预期中立调用的函数参数均用严格解析。对象键顺序或空白不同，但等价的 JSON 参数对象可以接受。

输出元数据存放在第一个 ToolCall 上的旧会话仍可回放。消息级和旧副本同时存在时，两者都必须有效且描述同一输出数组；数组只发送一次。新解码只使用消息级载体，避免存储两个副本。

不透明值被保留，本地不会独立认证。投影和副本验证检测历史不一致；加密推理认证仍由厂商端负责。

## 证据

使用 JDK 21 运行 `python harness-providers\target\responses-continuity-acceptance\verify.py`，依据现有 Surefire 依赖 classpath，在私有 target 目录编译当前核心源码、编辑后的 Responses 厂商和 JUnit 测试。结果：**13 项测试通过**。生成辅助脚本不是交付物。

覆盖：

- 新消息载体下有序加密推理和并行调用。
- 最终推理/文本回答随后经过真实 CodeAgent 检查点/恢复及用户追问，保留 phase 和不透明 annotations。
- 旧首调用回退与匹配双副本只回放一次。
- 可见文本/调用变化、格式错误和歧义 JSON、缺失加密推理、重复 ID、冲突副本，在再次 HTTP 请求前拒绝。
- 已有用量、未完成/拒绝、不支持输出及厂商中立历史契约。

所有请求均为 localhost。未运行 Maven 或真实/付费模型调用。负责人必须串行运行 reactor 完成组合验证。

## 修改的交付文件

- `harness-providers/src/main/java/dev/codeharness/providers/OpenAiResponsesProvider.java`
- `harness-providers/src/test/java/dev/codeharness/providers/OpenAiResponsesProviderTest.java`
- 本文档。

负责人提供参考：<https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning>（2026-10-14 获取，HTTP 200）。无状态推理要求历史中保留有序响应输出。已有 `store:false` 和受支持加密推理 include 保持不变。

# Local tokenizer budget accounting

Select `--token-counter cl100k` or `--token-counter o200k` on interactive/run/resume commands, or set `agent.token-counter` in trusted YAML. `utf16` remains the compatibility default. Unknown/null values fail before any model call or MCP launch. The selected counter applies to both registered schemas (including MCP) and conversation messages. It does not change output token limits.

```shell
harness.cmd run "Fix the failing parser" --token-counter o200k --context-budget 12000
```

The core exposes `InputTokenCounter` so other local accounting strategies can be supplied without coupling the provider-neutral loop to a JSON library or vendor tokenizer. The CLI uses bundled Jtokkit 1.1.0, ordinary tokenization with no special-token interpretation, and recursively sorted canonical JSON. Each entire message includes roles, tool identity, call JSON and opaque provider metadata. Tool definitions include descriptions and original schemas. An envelope reserve of 16 tokens and eight tokens per message are added; nonempty tools reserve 64 tokens plus eight per definition. These are explicit local reserves, not a claim to model a vendor's internal framing exactly.

Counts are summed over independently encoded records. They enforce the selected local accounting budget, not the exact vendor wire/billing token limit. A matching encoding and reserves improve on UTF-16 undercounting, especially for CJK, but Anthropic/Gemini/custom vendors may use different tokenizers or encodings. No vendor is inferred silently. Leave headroom for provider transformations, internal chat templates and output; consult actual usage in real evaluations.

Compaction measures candidates with the selected counter instead of assuming four characters save one token. BPE counts can be nonmonotonic when clipping text, so only candidates actually measured within budget are retained. System/original/latest user text, call arguments and signatures are never clipped; oversized required input fails locally. Messages with message-level or legacy call-level replay metadata keep their visible text intact so raw replay stays consistent. Complete optional historical blocks may still be removed. Text clipping respects UTF-16 surrogate pairs. Existing complete tool-cycle protection remains in force.

For speed, immutable message identities cache counts. The FIFO cache holds at most 256 entries and 1,048,576 serialized UTF-16 units; it stores references/counts, not extra source JSON. Oversized records are not cached. Registry encodings load lazily once per process. Cache eviction changes performance only, not counts; caches last one agent invocation and do not persist secrets.

Acceptance covers mandatory CJK instructions failing before model calls, bounded CJK/emoji tool results, independent serialized-array counts, retained opaque metadata, schema overhead, cache eviction and configuration/CLI rejection. The versioned context benchmark accepts `--token-counter cl100k` and `--token-counter o200k` to reproduce accounting, retention and warm-cache compaction timing. Cold tokenizer startup and real-model timing are outside that compaction measurement.

`python scripts/smoke_token_budget.py` uses the actual shaded jar and a localhost server to verify both CLI modes, legacy compatibility, and oversized mandatory CJK resume failing without an HTTP request.

# 本地分词器预算统计

在 interactive/run/resume 命令上选择 `--token-counter cl100k` 或 `--token-counter o200k`，也可在可信 YAML 中设置 `agent.token-counter`。`utf16` 仍为兼容性默认值。未知/null 值在模型调用或 MCP 启动之前失败。选定计数器同时作用于注册 schema（包括 MCP）和对话消息，不改变输出 token 上限。

```shell
harness.cmd run "修复失败的解析器" --token-counter o200k --context-budget 12000
```

核心公开 `InputTokenCounter`，可提供其他本地统计策略，不让厂商中立循环耦合 JSON 库或厂商分词器。CLI 使用随包 Jtokkit 1.1.0、无特殊 token 解释的普通分词，以及递归排序的规范 JSON。每条完整消息包括角色、工具身份、调用 JSON 和不透明厂商元数据。工具定义包含说明和原始 schema。添加 16 token 包络预留量、每条消息八 token；非空工具集预留 64 token，再加每个定义八 token。这些是显式本地预留量，不宣称精确模拟厂商内部消息框架。

各记录独立编码后求和。它们执行选定的本地统计预算，不是精确厂商传输/账单 token 上限。匹配编码和预留量可改善 UTF-16 低估，尤其是 CJK；Anthropic/Gemini/自定义厂商可能使用不同分词器或编码。不会静默推断厂商。请为厂商转换、内部聊天模板和输出预留空间，并参考真实评测中的实际用量。

压缩用选定计数器测量候选内容，不再假定四个字符节省一个 token。裁剪文本时 BPE 计数可能非单调，因此只保留实测在预算内的候选。系统/原始/最近用户文本、调用参数和签名绝不裁剪；过大的必需输入在本地失败。具有消息级或旧式调用级回放元数据的消息保留完整可见文本，以保持原始回放一致。完整的可选历史块仍可能被移除。文本裁剪尊重 UTF-16 代理对。已有完整工具循环保护仍生效。

为提高速度，不可变消息身份缓存计数。FIFO 缓存最多 256 项和 1,048,576 个序列化 UTF-16 单元；它保存引用/计数，不额外保存源码 JSON。过大记录不缓存。注册表编码每进程惰性加载一次。缓存淘汰只改变性能，不改变计数；缓存仅持续一次智能体调用，不持久化密钥。

验收覆盖必需 CJK 指令在模型调用前失败、有界 CJK/emoji 工具结果、独立序列化数组计数、不透明元数据保留、schema 开销、缓存淘汰和配置/CLI 拒绝。带版本的上下文基准接受 `--token-counter cl100k` 和 `--token-counter o200k`，复现统计、保留和热缓存压缩时间。冷分词器启动和真实模型时间不在此压缩测量范围内。

`python scripts/smoke_token_budget.py` 使用实际 shaded jar 和 localhost 服务验证两种 CLI 模式、旧式兼容性，以及过大的必需 CJK 恢复在无 HTTP 请求时失败。

# Local benchmark evidence

## Separately authorized CodeGo live acceptance, 2026-10-14

[codego-acceptance-v1.json](codego-acceptance-v1.json) records real calls to the user-supplied custom gateway with gpt-6-sol. The original six-row suite passed every independent code check but only five COMPLETED checks; a compact null/blank run reached its six-iteration limit. Matched completed pairs report 245,263 baseline / 71,304 compact input tokens, a 70.93% reduction for this seeded history workload. A separate changed-policy/eight-call-cap null/blank pair completed in two calls per variant and is excluded from that aggregate. Preliminary and strengthened workflow checks, gateway discovery and initial failures are also preserved. These are normalized gateway counts, not billing verification; first-text latency and stable production speed remain unmeasured. Earlier sections describe their historical localhost-only runs.

## Native streaming integration revalidation

`coding-evaluation-native-streaming.json` records the current rebuilt jar after native streaming: 12/12 independent Java checks and all positive/negative checker controls pass across 180 localhost requests. Baseline/compact cumulative cl100k payload counts are 1,317,290/242,768, with process medians 1430.249/1405.660 ms. This scripted fixture returns JSON despite stream requests and therefore verifies compatibility fallback plus context/tool correctness. It does not measure real generation or establish production speed/cost savings. Prior archives remain preserved.

## Bounded parallel reads

`parallel-reads-v1.json` records five samples per variant using eight 80 ms mock reads separated by a mutation barrier through real CodeAgent. Serial/four-read p50 is 741.024/184.2746 ms, p95 744.4713/185.5673 ms. Observed concurrency is one/four, all outputs and barrier checks pass, and both variants use two model requests and 3,255 serialized request bytes per sample. This isolates waiting-time overlap; it does not establish real-disk, provider or complete coding-task speedup or token savings. Reproduction and limitations: [parallel read benchmark](../PARALLEL_READ_BENCHMARK.md).

## Message metadata continuation, 2026-10-14

After message-level provider replay was integrated, sequential runs of both tokenizers passed exact existing fixture retention/pairing under the 1,200-token local message budget. See `context-cl100k-message-metadata.json` and `context-o200k-message-metadata.json`. After counts are 795/1160/376 (cl100k) and 798/1164/1117 (o200k), in code/diagnostic/multilingual order; warm-cache p50 spans 1.82–7.81 ms. The new serialized message field changes hashes/accounting, so prior archives are preserved rather than overwritten. These existing fixtures cover call metadata; message replay preservation and budget failure are separately covered by unit and packaged CLI acceptance. Prior paired coding results below were not rerun in this continuation. No real-vendor billing or latency claim is established.

Recorded on Windows 11 / Java 21.0.10 after the expired ten-hour window, 2026-10-14. All model traffic was localhost. No paid calls.

## Paired scripted Java repairs

Three tasks, two budgets and two order-alternating repetitions passed independent compile/assertion checks: 12/12. The checker rejected each buggy input and accepted its reference repair. Each actual CLI invocation made 15 mock requests; all retained current source before editing.

| Metric | Baseline (48000 estimate budget) | Compact (4000 estimate budget) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Passing independent checks | 6/6 | 6/6 |
| Cumulative serialized cl100k token count, all six runs | 1,315,310 | 240,788 |
| Cumulative serialized o200k token count | 1,317,396 | 241,818 |
| Cumulative serialized UTF-8 bytes | 5,363,502 | 1,034,754 |
| Median local CLI process elapsed, ms | 1389.39 | 1390.48 |

This specific scripted workload reduced serialized cl100k counts by 81.69%. This is not billed-token savings, AI coding-quality evidence or a production speedup. The policy uses fixed edits; provider usage is absent. Timing includes local JVM/process/checkpoint overhead and is too limited to infer a general speed difference.

## Context microbenchmark

| Context | cl100k before/after | o200k before/after | Compaction p50/p95 ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| code-history | 49,765 / 1,493 | 49,800 / 1,501 | 0.4662 / 1.0535 |
| diagnostic-history | 59,365 / 1,412 | 59,400 / 1,420 | 0.1264 / 0.2300 |
| multilingual-history | 98,729 / 3,338 | 67,564 / 2,458 | 0.1293 / 0.1492 |

All three cases retained exact instructions, current code, task/call metadata and paired tool results. Input fingerprints and raw metrics are in [context-benchmark.json](context-benchmark.json). The CJK case shows substantial UTF-16 underestimation; the configured estimate is not a tokenizer-enforced limit.

Raw paired runs: [coding-evaluation.json](coding-evaluation.json). Reproduction, semantics and opt-in live limitations: [BENCHMARKS.md](../BENCHMARKS.md). These files contain no credentials or private repository content.

## Tokenizer enforcement continuation (version 2)

Recorded after the final 2026-10-14 10:45:22 Asia/Shanghai reactor build. Both modes were measured sequentially after all tests/smokes/coding runs, without a concurrent build workload. All six cases preserve exact instructions, current source, opaque call metadata and paired results. The budget is 1,200 local message-accounting tokens; the fixed benchmark schema is excluded from that budget and included in serialized-payload reporting. CLI agent execution separately reserves registered schemas.

| Counter | Context | Local message count before/after | Warm-cache compaction p50/p95, ms |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| cl100k | code-history | 50,322 / 1,164 | 3.2947 / 5.2489 |
| cl100k | diagnostic-history | 59,922 / 1,110 | 1.9681 / 3.9227 |
| cl100k | multilingual-history | 99,286 / 346 | 5.6472 / 7.8664 |
| o200k | code-history | 50,354 / 1,168 | 3.7494 / 6.1372 |
| o200k | diagnostic-history | 59,954 / 1,114 | 2.7078 / 3.9740 |
| o200k | multilingual-history | 68,118 / 1,077 | 7.0676 / 8.2525 |

The tokenizer strategies cost additional local counting work compared with the historical UTF-16 approximation. These times include selected-counter compaction work and warm identity-cache behavior, and exclude encoding startup and final reporting tokenization. They establish local budget enforcement, not a latency improvement or exact vendor input limits. Fewer retained historical details do not prove equal performance on wider coding tasks.

Raw current reports: [context-cl100k-v2.json](context-cl100k-v2.json), [context-o200k-v2.json](context-o200k-v2.json). Historical version 1 above remains unchanged; its multilingual UTF-16 undercount is the gap addressed by explicit tokenizer modes.

## Multi-file workflow evaluation, 2026-10-14

`multifile-evaluation-v1.json` records 12 actual shaded-jar runs (three two-file repairs, baseline/compact budgets, two alternating repetitions) and 13 independent checker variants. All 12 passed. Each run validated 12 historical reads, source discovery/retention, a rejected stale hash without mutation, fresh cross-file edits, a real Java compile command, ordered results and a bounded change report; an unrelated source remained byte-identical. The checker compiled in a fresh directory with explicit classpath/sourcepath and no annotation processing, then ran 13 buggy/full/omitted-edit controls after the agent stopped.

| Metric | Baseline | Compact |
|---|---:|---:|
| Passing runs | 6/6 | 6/6 |
| Successful-pair serialized cl100k totals | 1,939,298 | 337,438 |
| Successful-pair serialized o200k totals | 1,942,896 | 339,312 |
| Successful-pair UTF-8 byte totals | 7,982,686 | 1,450,940 |
| Median local process elapsed, ms | 2,029.889 | 1,991.339 |

The compact fixture serialized 82.60% fewer cl100k tokens, 82.53% fewer o200k tokens and 81.82% fewer bytes for this fixed workload. These are canonical local message/schema counts with no provider usage; they are not billed savings, model-quality evidence or a production speed claim. The scripted policy supplies known repairs, and stale-edit recovery here is separate from process-crash resume recovery.

The rebuilt-jar [coding revalidation](coding-evaluation-revalidation.json) again passed 12/12 independent checks, all checker positive/negative controls and current-source retention, with 180 localhost requests. Serialized token/byte aggregates match the historical paired report exactly. Median process times were 1371.83 ms baseline and 1402.57 ms compact; no speedup or billed usage claim follows. This paired suite uses the unchanged default UTF-16 policy; tokenizer modes are separately verified by the six cases above and the packaged CJK fail-before-network smoke.

`parallel-reads-v1.json` 记录每种变体五个样本，使用真实 CodeAgent 执行八次 80 ms 模拟读取，并在中间设置修改屏障。串行/四路读取 p50 为 741.024/184.2746 ms，p95 为 744.4713/185.5673 ms。观测并发为一/四，全部输出和屏障检查通过；每个样本两种变体均使用两个模型请求和 3,255 序列化请求字节。它单独测量等待重叠，不能证明真实磁盘、厂商或完整编程任务提速或 token 节省。复现和限制见[并行读取基准](../PARALLEL_READ_BENCHMARK.md)。

## 多文件工作流评测，2026-10-14

`multifile-evaluation-v1.json` 记录 12 次实际 shaded jar 运行（三个双文件修复、基线/压缩预算、两次交替重复）和 13 个独立检查器变体。12 次全部通过。每次验证 12 次历史读取、源码发现/保留、无修改的过期哈希拒绝、新鲜跨文件编辑、真实 Java 编译命令、有序结果和有界变更报告；无关源码保持逐字节一致。检查器在新目录编译，显式设置 classpath/sourcepath，不执行注解处理，并在智能体停止后运行 13 个缺陷/完整/省略编辑对照。

# Context compaction review

## Changes

ContextCompactor now retains the original task, latest user instruction, every existing system message, latest assistant message, and latest complete tool exchange. Older assistant tool calls and their results are removed as indivisible blocks. Retained tool-call JSON is never shortened. Invalid histories with orphan, missing, or duplicate tool results fail locally with a bounded error.

Historical summaries use one assistant message containing bounded numeric counts only. They never include tool output, tool names, paths, arguments, or historical free-form instructions, and never create SYSTEM messages. Repeated compaction normalizes the summary to one message and is idempotent when the input and limits are unchanged.

When indispensable context still exceeds the configured estimate after optional text is shortened, compaction throws a bounded error without echoing source text. This lets the agent fail before issuing an oversized model request. The estimate includes call IDs and tool-result metadata, but remains an approximation rather than a provider tokenizer.

## Validation

Core Maven test suite: 27 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors. The focused ContextCompactorTest suite has 9 tests covering system/task/latest-intent preservation, paired and multi-tool exchanges, strict oversized-context failures, malformed history, idempotency across repeated calls and new turns, and bounded summary counts. Existing recovery and boundary tests also pass.

Command equivalent: mvn -pl harness-core test -DforkCount=0. Tests ran via the Java 21 Maven launcher because exec_command fails on this host with a Windows CET startup error. Evidence: harness-core/target/core-audit-test.log.

## Deterministic context-size fixture

A transcript containing two system messages, one original task, and 40 tool exchanges with repeated large text produced:

| Metric | Local estimate |
|---|---:|
| Before compaction | 240,831 |
| After compaction | 448 |
| Configured budget | 500 |

Assertions verify that both system messages and the original task are unchanged, the latest tool exchange remains paired, every retained call/result is paired, repeated compaction is unchanged, and the result fits the configured estimate. This synthetic repeated-output fixture demonstrates bounded context reduction only. It does not measure real API token savings, coding success rate, latency, or tokenization accuracy.

## Tradeoffs and remaining scope

The numeric summary intentionally omits historical details; the agent may need to reread source files. Original task and latest instruction are preserved, while intermediate user turns may be removed. Oversized indispensable tool arguments cause an explicit failure rather than JSON corruption. Provider-native token accounting and output reservation remain separate concerns. No other production classes were edited during this scoped follow-up.

# 上下文压缩评审

## 变更

ContextCompactor 现在保留原始任务、最近用户指令、所有已有系统消息、最近助手消息和最近完整工具交互。较旧助手工具调用及其结果作为不可拆分块移除。保留的工具调用 JSON 绝不缩短。孤立、缺失或重复工具结果的无效历史以有界错误在本地失败。

历史摘要使用一条助手消息，只含有界数字计数。它绝不包含工具输出、工具名称、路径、参数或历史自由文本指令，绝不创建 SYSTEM 消息。重复压缩把摘要规范化为一条消息；输入和限制未变时保持幂等。

缩短可选文本后，不可缺少的上下文若仍超过配置估算，压缩抛出有界错误，不回显源码文本。智能体因此可在发送过大模型请求前失败。估算包含调用 ID 和工具结果元数据，但仍是近似值，不是厂商分词器。

## 验证

核心 Maven 测试套件：27 项测试、0 失败、0 错误。针对性的 ContextCompactorTest 有 9 项，覆盖系统/任务/最近意图保留、配对和多工具交互、严格过大上下文失败、错误历史、重复调用和新轮次间幂等，以及有界摘要计数。已有恢复和边界测试也通过。

等价命令：mvn -pl harness-core test -DforkCount=0。测试通过 Java 21 Maven 启动器执行，因为当时此宿主上的 exec_command 因 Windows CET 启动错误失败。证据：harness-core/target/core-audit-test.log。

## 确定性上下文大小夹具

包含两条系统消息、一个原始任务和 40 次重复大文本工具交互的记录产生：

| 测量项 | 本地估算 |
|---|---:|
| 压缩前 | 240,831 |
| 压缩后 | 448 |
| 配置预算 | 500 |

断言验证两条系统消息和原始任务不变、最近工具交互仍配对、每个保留调用/结果配对、重复压缩不变，并且结果符合配置估算。此合成重复输出夹具只证明上下文减少受限；不测量真实 API token 节省、编程成功率、延迟或分词准确度。

## 取舍与剩余范围

数字摘要有意省略历史细节；智能体可能需要重新读取源码文件。原始任务和最近指令保留，中间用户轮次可能移除。过大的不可缺少工具参数会明确失败，避免损坏 JSON。厂商原生 token 统计和输出预留是独立问题。此次限定范围的后续工作没有修改其他生产类。

# Portable CLI installation

Extract the complete archive to any directory. Java 21 or later must be installed; a JDK is needed to compile Java projects. Runtime dependencies are included in `lib/harness.jar`. Maven and Python are not required to run this distribution.

On Windows, invoke `C:\path\to\distribution\bin\harness.cmd --help`. On Linux/macOS, invoke `/path/to/distribution/bin/harness --help` (or `sh /path/to/distribution/bin/harness --help` if an unzip tool dropped executable permissions). Launchers use `JAVA_HOME/bin/java` when JAVA_HOME is set, otherwise java from PATH. Keep the bin/lib layout intact. You may add the bin directory to PATH; launch from your code repository or pass `--workspace` explicitly. The launcher does not change your current directory.

Run `harness doctor` and `harness providers` to check local setup without contacting a model. Copy `config.example.yaml` to a chosen configuration path, select a provider/model and set the named credential environment variable. Pass `--config /path/to/config.yaml`. See README.md for all options, provider caveats, permissions and session recovery.

Examples (use harness.cmd instead of harness on Windows):

```shell
harness --config /path/to/config.yaml --workspace /path/to/project
harness --config /path/to/config.yaml --workspace /path/to/project run "Fix the parser and verify it"
harness --config /path/to/config.yaml --workspace /path/to/project resume SESSION_ID "Handle empty input too"
```

The bundled example is not automatically loaded. Workspaces, credentials and sessions are not bundled. Custom provider jars can be used with `java -cp` and `dev.codeharness.cli.HarnessCli`; see README.md.

`manifest.json` records SHA-256 values for the contained files. The outer SHA256SUMS records each archive's checksum; neither is a signature or proof of publisher identity. Build/acceptance evidence and known limitations are in WORKPLAN.md. This is a local snapshot distribution; real-vendor and Linux acceptance remain unverified.
